title: Head and Starc out of IPL squads as Cummins and Green stay
image_query: Rajiv Gandhi International Cricket Stadium Hyderabad
excerpt: Travis Head will skip IPL 2027 and Mitchell Starc has been released, but Pat Cummins and Cameron Green have kept their places.
content_html:
Two of Australia's best-known white-ball cricketers are missing from Indian Premier League squads for 2027 after franchises confirmed their retained and released players on 17 November.

Sunrisers Hyderabad released opener Travis Head, who had been on a ₹14 crore contract, after the left-hander chose to skip next season. Reports linked his decision to managing his workload around Australia's crowded international calendar, including Ashes commitments.

Head was one of nine players released by Sunrisers, a list that also included South African fast bowler Gerald Coetzee and Sri Lankan all-rounder Kamindu Mendis.

Delhi Capitals also released veteran fast bowler Mitchell Starc.

Not a full exodus

Other Australians stayed put. Sunrisers kept captain Pat Cummins, and Kolkata Knight Riders retained all-rounder Cameron Green.

Green's retention was one of the talking points of the window. Kolkata signed him for ₹25.20 crore before the 2026 season, making him the most expensive overseas player in IPL history. He scored 322 runs in 14 matches at an average of 32.20 and a strike rate of 145.70, a return some commentators felt fell short of the price.

The workload question

Australian players carry one of the heaviest schedules in world cricket, and the IPL is played in March to May, straight after the home summer. The pull between national duty and franchise money is not new, but releases of this size suggest some senior players are choosing rest over large pay cheques.

Indian outlets reported that uncertainty over Australian availability could also shape how other franchises plan their spending.

What's next

Neither player is barred from future seasons. Released players who want to play in 2027 must register for the mini-auction, which will be held in Goa on 16 December.

Across the ten teams, 184 players were retained, including 55 from overseas, leaving 66 places to fill at the auction.

Other big moves

The Australians were not the only high-profile names cut loose. Mumbai Indians released New Zealand quick Trent Boult, Indian seamer Deepak Chahar and South African spinner Keshav Maharaj, while keeping Rohit Sharma, Suryakumar Yadav, Jasprit Bumrah and Tilak Varma. Chennai Super Kings confirmed that former captain MS Dhoni had retired as a player. Royal Challengers Bengaluru go into the new season as defending champions.
